## Goal

Notebook 05 rebuilt the ingredients of the authors' input from public data: the same cells and counts exactly, and a
gene selection that recovers 92 % of theirs (160 of 174 genes, Jaccard index 0.89; protocol B+). Here we assemble these ingredients into a mosaic table, run
MIIC with the authors' settings, and compare the resulting network with the published one.

Our mosaic differs from the authors' in two ways only:

1. **the selected genes**: about 160 of the authors' 174 selected genes, plus 7 others (notebook 05, section 8);
2. **no duplicated columns**: each gene appears once per cell type, always named `<gene>_<cell type>`.

Everything else is kept identical, so that differences can be attributed to these two points: same cells, in the same
row order as the authors' table; same metadata; same 43 L-R pairs; same MIIC settings and the same rule for declaring a
variable discrete.

**Inputs:** `results/case2/05_rebuild_input/rebuild_inputs.rds` (written by notebook 05) and the authors' files in
`data/case2/causalccc_server_w0788tM1wzXGHLzNaKKa/`.
**Outputs:** `results/case2/06_rebuilt_network/`: our input files (`input.tsv`, `state_order.tsv`,
`interact_edges.tsv`), the MIIC result (`miic_result.rds`) and our edge list (`edges.tsv`).

::: {.callout-note}
## Running time
The MIIC run takes about three hours (notebook 04: 2.8 hours on one thread). The result is saved the first time and reloaded
afterwards. To force a new run, delete `results/case2/06_rebuilt_network/miic_result.rds`.
:::

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(miic)

root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))) {
  if (dirname(root) == root) stop("Repository root not found. Open the repository folder in Positron.")
  root <- dirname(root)
}
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

job_dir     <- file.path(root, "data", "case2", "causalccc_server_w0788tM1wzXGHLzNaKKa")
inputs_file <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "05_rebuild_input", "rebuild_inputs.rds")
results_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "case2", "06_rebuilt_network")

if (!file.exists(inputs_file)) stop("Run notebook 05 first: it writes ", inputs_file)
dir.create(results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cell_types <- c("Fibroblasts", "T_cell", "DCs")
strip      <- function(v) str_remove_all(v, "_(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)")
```

## 1. Ingredients

```{r}
#| label: ingredients

rebuilt     <- readRDS(inputs_file)
counts      <- rebuilt$counts
meta        <- rebuilt$meta
match_cells <- rebuilt$match_cells   # one row per row of the authors' table, with the matching cell
lr_roles    <- rebuilt$lr_roles      # ligands and receptors of each cell type

# The authors' files, for the metadata levels, the L-R pairs and the comparison
mosaic_authors <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "input.tsv"), guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = FALSE)
state_authors  <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "clean_state_order.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
lr_pairs       <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "clean_interact_edges.tsv"),
                           col_names = c("ligand", "receptor"), show_col_types = FALSE)
edges_authors  <- read_tsv(file.path(job_dir, "edgesList.miic.summary.txt"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

The genes of each cell type: its ligands and receptors, plus the genes selected by protocol B+ (without the metadata,
which are added separately).

```{r}
#| label: genes

genes <- map(set_names(cell_types), \(t) {
  unique(c(lr_roles$gene[lr_roles$cell_type == t],
           setdiff(rebuilt$selection[[t]], c("labels", "condition"))))
})

lengths(genes)
```

## 2. Build the mosaic table

Rows: the cells, in the order of the authors' table (`match_cells` is sorted by authors' row). Columns: for each cell
type, its genes named `<gene>_<cell type>` and its two metadata `labels_<cell type>` and `condition_<cell type>`. Each
cell has values only in the columns of its type, `NA` elsewhere.

```{r}
#| label: mosaic

match_cells <- arrange(match_cells, row)

blocks <- map(cell_types, \(t) {
  in_type <- match_cells$cell_type == t
  cells   <- match_cells$cell[in_type]

  values <- as.matrix(counts[genes[[t]], cells, drop = FALSE]) |> t() |> as_tibble()
  names(values) <- paste0(genes[[t]], "_", t)
  values[[paste0("labels_", t)]]    <- meta$labels[cells]
  values[[paste0("condition_", t)]] <- meta$condition[cells]

  # place the block in the rows of its cell type, NA in the other rows
  full <- values[rep(NA_integer_, nrow(match_cells)), ]
  full[in_type, ] <- values
  full
})

mosaic <- bind_cols(blocks)
dim(mosaic)

# Same structure checks as in notebook 03: each block complete, everything else empty
row_type <- match_cells$cell_type
col_type <- column_cell_type(mosaic, row_type)
map(cell_types, \(t) tibble(cell_type = t,
                           own_block_complete = !anyNA(mosaic[row_type == t, col_type == t]),
                           elsewhere_empty    = all(is.na(mosaic[row_type == t, col_type != t])))) |>
  list_rbind()

# No duplicated column in any cell type
map_int(cell_types, \(t) sum(duplicated(as.list(mosaic[row_type == t, col_type == t]))))
```

For the genes that the authors also used, are our values the authors' values? We compare, for each such variable, the
authors' column with ours (the rows are in the same order).

```{r}
#| label: same-values

authors_vars <- tibble(variable_authors = names(mosaic_authors),
                       cell_type = column_cell_type(mosaic_authors, row_type)) |>
  mutate(variable = if_else(str_detect(variable_authors, "^(labels|condition)_"),
                            variable_authors, paste0(strip(variable_authors), "_", cell_type))) |>
  filter(variable %in% names(mosaic))

authors_vars |>
  mutate(identical = map2_lgl(variable_authors, variable, \(a, o) identical(as.character(mosaic_authors[[a]]),
                                                                            as.character(mosaic[[o]])))) |>
  count(identical)
```

## 3. State order and L-R pairs

The same rules as the authors' files: metadata discrete with the authors' order of levels; a gene discrete if it has
5 or fewer distinct values counting `NA` (the rule of `causalCCC.state_order()`, notebook 02), continuous otherwise;
groups `ligands`, `receptors`, `<cell type> genes` and `metadata`, with the authors' colours.

```{r}
#| label: state-order

role_of <- lr_roles |> transmute(variable = paste0(gene, "_", cell_type), role)

group_colours <- state_authors |> distinct(group, group_color)

state_order <- tibble(var_names = names(mosaic), cell_type = col_type) |>
  left_join(role_of, by = c("var_names" = "variable")) |>
  mutate(is_metadata = str_detect(var_names, "^(labels|condition)_"),
         group = case_when(is_metadata    ~ "metadata",
                           role == "ligand"   ~ "ligands",
                           role == "receptor" ~ "receptors",
                           .default = paste(cell_type, "genes")),
         var_type = if_else(map_lgl(mosaic, is.character) | map_int(mosaic, n_distinct) <= 5, 0, 1),
         is_contextual = 0) |>
  left_join(select(state_authors, var_names, levels_increasing_order), by = "var_names") |>
  left_join(group_colours, by = "group") |>
  select(var_names, var_type, levels_increasing_order, is_contextual, group, group_color)

count(state_order, group, var_type)

# The 43 L-R pairs, with our variable names (identical to the authors' names for these genes)
interact_edges <- lr_pairs |>
  mutate(cell_l = column_cell_type(mosaic_authors, row_type)[ligand],
         cell_r = column_cell_type(mosaic_authors, row_type)[receptor],
         ligand   = paste0(strip(ligand), "_", cell_l),
         receptor = paste0(strip(receptor), "_", cell_r)) |>
  select(ligand, receptor)

all(c(interact_edges$ligand, interact_edges$receptor) %in% names(mosaic))
```

We save the three input files, in the format of the CausalCCC server, so that the same run can be repeated elsewhere
(for example on a computing cluster, or uploaded to the web server).

```{r}
#| label: write-inputs

write_tsv(mosaic, file.path(results_dir, "input.tsv"), na = "NA")
write_tsv(state_order, file.path(results_dir, "state_order.tsv"), na = "NA")
write_tsv(interact_edges, file.path(results_dir, "interact_edges.tsv"), col_names = FALSE)
```

## 4. Run MIIC (or reload the saved result)

The same call as in notebook 04, on one thread like the server. (A first attempt with 4 threads crashed at the start
of the run with C stack errors: the multithreading of this `miic` branch is not reliable.)

```{r}
#| label: run-miic
#| results: hide

result_file <- file.path(results_dir, "miic_result.rds")

if (file.exists(result_file)) {
  miic_result <- readRDS(result_file)
  message("Loaded the saved result from ", result_file)
} else {
  set.seed(2026)
  start <- Sys.time()
  miic_result <- miic(
    input_data      = as.data.frame(mosaic),
    state_order     = as.data.frame(state_order),
    interact_edges  = as.data.frame(interact_edges),
    cplx            = "nml",
    orientation     = TRUE,
    latent          = "orientation",
    ori_proba_ratio = 0.01,
    n_shuffles      = 100,
    conf_threshold  = 0.01,
    test_mar        = TRUE,
    consistent      = "no",
    n_eff           = -1,
    mode            = "S",
    n_threads       = 1
  )
  attr(miic_result, "run_time") <- Sys.time() - start
  saveRDS(miic_result, result_file)
}

lr_links <- link_name(interact_edges$ligand, interact_edges$receptor)

edges_ours <- as_tibble(miic_result$all.edges.summary) |>
  filter(!(link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links & Nxy_ai %in% 0))   # remove the L-R placeholder rows (notebook 02)

write_tsv(edges_ours, file.path(results_dir, "edges.tsv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: run-time

attr(miic_result, "run_time")
```

## 5. Compare with the authors' network

To compare the two networks, each variable is identified by its gene and its cell type (`gene | cell type`). In the
authors' network, the two copies of a duplicated gene become the same node, and the link between them disappears.

```{r}
#| label: node-keys

key_of_authors <- tibble(variable = names(mosaic_authors),
                         cell_type = column_cell_type(mosaic_authors, row_type)) |>
  mutate(key = if_else(str_detect(variable, "^(labels|condition)_"), variable,
                       paste0(strip(variable), "_", cell_type))) |>
  pull(key, name = variable)

type_of_key <- function(k) str_extract(k, "(Fibroblasts|T_cell|DCs)$")

as_links <- function(edge_list, key_of) {
  edge_list |>
    filter(type == "P") |>
    mutate(a = key_of[x], b = key_of[y]) |>
    filter(a != b) |>
    transmute(link = link_name(a, b), a, b,
              cell_type = if_else(type_of_key(a) == type_of_key(b), type_of_key(a), "L-R")) |>
    distinct(link, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

key_of_ours <- set_names(names(mosaic))   # our names are already keys

links_authors <- as_links(edges_authors, key_of_authors)
links_ours    <- as_links(edges_ours, key_of_ours)

tibble(network = c("authors", "ours"),
       variables = c(n_distinct(key_of_authors), ncol(mosaic)),
       links = c(nrow(links_authors), nrow(links_ours)))
```

A link can only be found in both networks if both its genes are in both inputs. We therefore compare the links among
the variables shared by the two inputs.

```{r}
#| label: compare-links

shared_vars <- intersect(unique(key_of_authors), names(mosaic))
length(shared_vars)

comparison <- full_join(
  links_authors |> filter(a %in% shared_vars, b %in% shared_vars) |> mutate(authors = TRUE),
  links_ours    |> filter(a %in% shared_vars, b %in% shared_vars) |> mutate(ours = TRUE),
  by = c("link", "a", "b", "cell_type")) |>
  mutate(found_in = case_when(!is.na(authors) & !is.na(ours) ~ "both",
                              !is.na(authors)                ~ "authors only",
                              .default                       = "ours only"))

comparison |>
  count(cell_type, found_in) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = found_in, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(jaccard = both / (both + `authors only` + `ours only`))
```

**Orientations.** How many retained links are oriented, bidirected, or genuine causations, in each network (L-R links
excluded, since they are oriented by construction)?

```{r}
#| label: orientations

orientation_summary <- function(edge_list, lr, network) {
  edge_list |>
    filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr) |>
    summarise(network = network, links = n(),
              not_oriented = sum(infOrt == 1), oriented = sum(abs(infOrt) == 2), bidirected = sum(infOrt == 6),
              genuine_causation = sum(is_causal == "Y"))
}

bind_rows(orientation_summary(edges_authors, link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor), "authors"),
          orientation_summary(edges_ours, lr_links, "ours"))
```

The authors' counts include the links of duplicated genes (each neighbour linked to both copies). For a fair
comparison, we look at the orientation of the gene–gene links found in **both** networks, written from the first to the
second gene of the link name (2 = first → second, −2 = second → first, 1 = not oriented, 6 = bidirected).

```{r}
#| label: shared-orientations

oriented_links <- function(edge_list, key_of, lr) {
  edge_list |>
    filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr) |>
    mutate(a = key_of[x], b = key_of[y]) |>
    filter(a != b) |>
    transmute(link = link_name(a, b),
              orientation = if_else(a == pmin(a, b) | infOrt %in% c(1, 6), infOrt, -infOrt),
              is_causal) |>
    distinct(link, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

shared_orientation <- inner_join(
  oriented_links(edges_authors, key_of_authors, link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor)),
  oriented_links(edges_ours, key_of_ours, lr_links),
  by = "link", suffix = c("_authors", "_ours"))

nrow(shared_orientation)
table(authors = shared_orientation$orientation_authors, ours = shared_orientation$orientation_ours)
table(authors = shared_orientation$is_causal_authors, ours = shared_orientation$is_causal_ours)
```

**Strength of the L-R links**, which the `causalccc` branch sets to the strongest link of the network:

```{r}
#| label: lr-strength

c(authors = max(edges_authors$info_shifted[edges_authors$type == "P"]),
  ours    = max(edges_ours$info_shifted[edges_ours$type == "P"]))

edges_ours |> filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links) |> slice_max(info_shifted, n = 3) |>
  select(x, y, info_shifted)
```

## 6. Do the paper's statements hold in our network?

The checks of notebook 03 (section 6), with our variable names.

```{r}
#| label: claims

intracellular_ours <- edges_ours |> filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links)

claims <- tribble(
  ~centre,              ~gene,
  "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "DCN_Fibroblasts",
  "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "APOD_Fibroblasts",
  "CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "CFD_Fibroblasts",
  "CXCR4_DCs",          "GPR183_DCs",
  "CXCR4_DCs",          "NR4A3_DCs",
  "CXCR4_DCs",          "VIM_DCs",
  "CXCR4_T_cell",       "FOS_T_cell",
  "CXCR4_T_cell",       "JUNB_T_cell"
)

claims |>
  mutate(in_our_input = gene %in% names(mosaic),
         distance_ours = map2_dbl(centre, gene, \(c, g) unname(graph_distance(intracellular_ours, c)[g])))
```

For comparison, the distances in the authors' network (notebook 03): DCN 2, APOD 2, CFD 1; GPR183 2, NR4A3 1, VIM 2;
FOS 2, JUNB 1.

**Direct neighbours** of CXCL12 and CXCR4 in both networks:

```{r}
#| label: neighbours

intracellular_authors <- edges_authors |> filter(type == "P", !link_name(x, y) %in% link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor))

map(c("CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "CXCR4_DCs", "CXCR4_T_cell"), \(c) {
  tibble(centre  = c,
         authors = paste(sort(key_of_authors[neighbors_of(c, intracellular_authors)$neighbor]), collapse = ", "),
         ours    = paste(sort(neighbors_of(c, intracellular_ours)$neighbor), collapse = ", "))
}) |> list_rbind()
```

## 7. The Figure 3C neighbourhood, drawn

Figure 3C of the paper shows the second-degree neighbourhood of the CXCL12–CXCR4 links: all genes at most two
intracellular links away from CXCL12 in fibroblasts or from CXCR4 in dendritic cells and T cells. We draw it for the
authors' network and for ours with `plot_neighbourhood()` (in `scripts/helpers.R`).

How to read the drawings: diamonds are CXCL12 and the two CXCR4; colours are cell types; dashed lines are the given L-R
links (drawn thin, since their strength is set artificially); an arrowhead is an orientation found by MIIC, and a green
link a genuine causation; thicker links are stronger. A star marks the duplicated columns of the authors' table
(notebook 03), and "subtype" is the metadata `labels`. The drawings are interactive: hover over a node or a link for
details, click a node to highlight its neighbours, drag to rearrange, scroll to zoom.

```{r}
#| label: drawing-inputs

centres          <- c("CXCL12_Fibroblasts", "CXCR4_DCs", "CXCR4_T_cell")
lr_links_authors <- link_name(lr_pairs$ligand, lr_pairs$receptor)
copies_authors   <- duplicated_columns(mosaic_authors, row_type, column_cell_type(mosaic_authors, row_type))
type_of_authors  <- set_names(type_of_key(key_of_authors), names(key_of_authors))
type_of_ours     <- set_names(type_of_key(names(mosaic)), names(mosaic))
label_authors    <- \(v) gene_label(v, copies_authors)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-3c-authors

plot_neighbourhood(edges_authors, lr_links_authors, centres, type_of_authors, label_authors,
                   title = "Authors' network")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-3c-ours

plot_neighbourhood(edges_ours, lr_links, centres, type_of_ours, gene_label,
                   title = "Our network (rebuilt input)")
```


## What we learned

**The skeleton of the network is robust.** Our input has 217 variables instead of the authors' 238 (224 once their
duplicates are merged), and 210 variables are shared. Among them, most links are found by both runs: Jaccard index
0.92 within T cells, 0.89 within fibroblasts and 0.85 within dendritic cells. Our run took 1.1 hours (2.8 hours for the
authors' input): fewer variables, and no duplicated columns.

**Figure 3 is reproduced.** The direct neighbours of CXCL12 in fibroblasts (APOE, C3, CFD, CFH, CXCL14) and of CXCR4
in dendritic cells (NR4A3, RGS1, UBC) and in T cells (JUNB, ZFP36) are exactly the same, and every gene named in the
paper is at the same distance as in the authors' network (CFD, NR4A3, JUNB direct; DCN, APOD, GPR183, VIM, FOS at two
links).

**Orientations: mostly robust, genuine causations less so.** On the 461 gene–gene links found in both networks, the
table above gives 79 % with the same orientation status. That figure is biased: in the authors' network, a link of one of
the 14 duplicated genes appears once per copy, the two copies often get different orientations, and the comparison keeps
one copy (notebook 07, section 5). On the 361 shared links that involve no duplicated gene, **96 % keep their
orientation and none is reversed**; against the authors' network without duplicates, 94 % of all 461 shared links keep
their orientation (notebook 07). Genuine causations are less stable: on these 361 links, the authors' network has 14 and
ours 12, with only 8 in common. The CXCL12 → CFD orientation of the authors' network, for example, is not found.
Orientations, and the "upstream"/"downstream" reading they support, should be interpreted with more caution than the
presence of links.

**L-R link strength.** Without duplicates, the strongest link of the network is S100A10–S100A6 in fibroblasts (3,050
instead of 11,579 for the two copies of S100A6). Since the `causalccc` branch gives every L-R link the strength of the
strongest link, the L-R strengths of the published network were set by a duplicated gene.

**Overall, for case study 2.** The input of this notebook (protocol B+) differs from the authors' by a handful of genes
near the selection cut-off and by the duplicated columns. The links of the published network, and the Figure 3
neighbourhoods, are reproduced; the orientations are only partly reproduced. Notebook 07 then shows that the gene
differences come from the selection settings (25 genes per run, no cap of 8, both metadata), which reproduce the
authors' genes exactly, and that the duplicated columns change no link and no orientation outside the links of the
14 duplicated genes, whose two copies are often oriented differently.
